# omada_site (Resource)

Manages an Omada site: the top-level container a network administrator creates to manage the devices and clients at a specific physical location.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "omada_site" "example" {
  name      = "Example Branch Office"
  region    = "United States"
  timezone  = "America/Chicago"
  address   = "123 Main St, Springfield, IL"
  latitude  = 39.7817
  longitude = -89.6501
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the site. Must be 1 to 64 characters.

### Optional

- `address` (String) Street address of the site.
- `latitude` (Number) Latitude of the site, within the range -90 to 90.
- `longitude` (Number) Longitude of the site, within the range -180 to 180.
- `region` (String) Country/region of the site, as an ISO country code abbreviation (e.g. `United States` for the United States of America).
- `scenario` (String) Deployment scenario of the site. See the controller's "Get scenario list" interface for accepted values.
- `support_es` (Boolean) Whether the site supports adopting Agile (ES) series switches.
- `support_l2` (Boolean) Whether the site supports adopting non-Agile (L2) series switches.
- `tag_ids` (List of String) IDs of the site tags applied to this site. Tag IDs are created via the controller's site tag endpoints.
- `timezone` (String) Timezone of the site. See section 5.1 of the Omada Open API Access Guide for accepted values.
- `type` (Number) Type of the site: `0` for a basic site, `1` for a pro site. Defaults to `0`. Cannot be changed after creation; changing it forces recreation.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Site ID assigned by the controller.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Sites can be imported using their site ID, as assigned by the controller.
terraform import omada_site.example <site_id>
```
